Objective Frame

Source: R/objClass.R
objframe.Rd

An objective frame stores residuals and their derivatives with respect to parameters, as res() returns them.

Usage

objframe(
  mydata,
  deriv = NULL,
  deriv.err = NULL,
  deriv2 = NULL,
  deriv2.err = NULL
)

Arguments

mydata

Data frame with columns time, name, value, prediction, sigma, residual, weighted.residual, bloq and weighted.0; further columns are dropped.

deriv

numeric matrix [n_residuals, p] of first-order derivatives of the residuals

deriv.err

numeric matrix [n_residuals, p] of first-order derivatives of the error model

deriv2

numeric 3D array [n_residuals, p, p] of second-order derivatives of residuals with respect to parameters. Optional.

deriv2.err

numeric 3D array [n_residuals, p, p] of second-order derivatives of the error model. Optional.

Value

An object of class "objframe" (data.table) with attributes "deriv" and "deriv.err". These arrays have the same parameter axes as those returned by prdframe and res. When deriv2/deriv2.err are supplied, the corresponding 3D arrays are attached as "deriv2" / "deriv2.err".

Examples

## Prediction with the derivative of the observable y in the parameter k
times <- 0:2
J <- array(-times * exp(-times), c(3, 1, 1), list(NULL, "y", "k"))
out <- prdframe(cbind(time = times, y = exp(-times)), deriv = J, parameters = c(k = 1))

data <- data.frame(time = times, name = "y", value = c(1.05, 0.35, 0.15),
                   sigma = 0.1, lloq = -Inf)
r <- res(data, out)
r
#>     time   name value prediction sigma    residual weighted.residual   bloq
#>    <int> <char> <num>      <num> <num>       <num>             <num> <lgcl>
#> 1:     0      y  1.05  1.0000000   0.1 -0.05000000        -0.5000000  FALSE
#> 2:     1      y  0.35  0.3678794   0.1  0.01787944         0.1787944  FALSE
#> 3:     2      y  0.15  0.1353353   0.1 -0.01466472        -0.1466472  FALSE
#>    weighted.0
#>         <num>
#> 1:  10.000000
#> 2:   3.678794
#> 3:   1.353353
attr(r, "deriv")
#>               k
#> [1,]  0.0000000
#> [2,] -0.3678794
#> [3,] -0.2706706
